KORAL.title: Ion Selection
KORAL.content:
# Ion Selection

- **Identify the ion:** Enter the ion atomic number, choose the ion name from the element list, or enter the chemical symbol; selecting **PT** opens the periodic table, where any ion can be selected by mouse click.
- **Enter the ion mass:** TRIM defaults to the mass of the most abundant isotope (MAI) for the selected element (shown in the periodic table), but any mass may be entered (units: amu).
- **Enter the ion energy:** Specify the ion energy in keV; TRIM accepts values up to 10,000,000 keV/amu, but for energies above 1,000 keV/amu, nuclear reaction energy losses are not included, so significant inelastic losses may be omitted.

KORAL.title: Target Data
KORAL.content:
## Target Data

- Enter the target elements: Use the PT button to open the periodic table and select elements by mouse click; if the target contains more than one element, press Add Element for each.
- Target constraints: Only homogeneous targets are supported; layered structures are not allowed.
- Compounds: A large list of common compounds is available in the Compound Dictionary, including special stopping powers for many compounds.
- Stoichiometry and density: For compounds, enter the relative atomic stoichiometry of each element; when finished, carefully review the target density, since ion ranges are linearly dependent on target density.

KORAL.title: Model Selection
KORAL.content:
# Model Selection

- Select the **electronic stopping model** used for the simulation.
- Available models depend on ion type and energy range.

## Typical Options
- Standard SRIM stopping model
- Experimental or user-modified stopping tables

> Hint: Changing the stopping model directly affects projected range and straggling.

KORAL.title: Output Options
KORAL.content:
# Output Options

- Choose which physical quantities are calculated and stored.
- Enable or disable detailed output tables and plots.

## Common Outputs
- Stopping power vs depth
- Projected range and longitudinal straggling
- Energy loss distributions

> Hint: Disabling unused outputs can significantly reduce computation time.

KORAL.title: Range / Straggling vs Energy
KORAL.content:
# Range / Straggling vs Energy

- Define an **energy range** for the ion simulation.
- The simulation computes projected range and straggling for each energy step.

## Controls
- Start energy
- End energy
- Energy step size

> Hint: Use smaller energy steps for smoother curves, especially at low energies.

MC Setup.title: Ion Selection
MC Setup.content:
# Ion Selection (MC Setup)

- Select the incident ion using the **Periodic Table** button.
- Check **Z**, **symbol**, and **mass (amu)**.
- Set the incident **energy (keV)** in the Ion Selection box.

## Angle of incidence
- The **angle of incidence** is configured in **Advanced Options** (⚙).
- MC Setup and KORAL can use **different angles**.

> Hint: Make sure the ion mass matches your intended isotope.

MC Setup.title: Target Layer Selection
MC Setup.content:
# Target Layer Selection

This table defines the target stack the ion traverses.

## Typical fields
- **Name**: free label for the layer
- **Width + unit**: layer thickness
- **Density**: material density used in the simulation
- **Compound correction**: correction factor (if applicable)
- **Gas**: marks the layer as a gas

## Behavior
- The currently selected layer controls which entries you edit in **Atoms per layer**.
- Gas layers enforce **solid-state energy parameters = 0** (damage/disp/latt/surf).

> Hint: Use gas layers for low-density targets; don’t mix gas with solid-state parameters.

MC Setup.title: Atoms per Layer
MC Setup.content:
# Atoms per layer

Defines the **composition of the currently selected target layer**.

## Editing
- Use the element picker to add an element to the layer.
- Use `+` / `-` to add/remove entries.
- Edit the **ratio / stoichiometry** values directly.

## Energy parameters
- **Damage / Disp / Latt / Surf (eV)** can be shown/hidden from **Advanced Options**.
- If a layer is marked as **Gas**, these values are forced to **0**.

> Hint: Stoichiometry is typically normalized internally; ensure your ratios are meaningful (sum > 0).

MC Setup.title: Model Selection
MC Setup.content:
# Model selection

Select the physical model(s) used by the simulator (e.g. stopping / scattering model).

## Notes
- Different models can produce noticeably different ranges and straggling.
- If results look unexpected, re-check model selection first.

> Hint: Keep the model consistent when comparing runs.

MC Setup.title: Simulator Selection
MC Setup.content:
# Simulator selection

Choose which backend runs the Monte Carlo simulation.

## Options
- **OpenTRIM**: OpenTRIM-based simulator
- **PyTRIM**: Python implementation

> Hint: If performance or outputs differ, try the other simulator to cross-check.

MC Setup.title: Output Options
MC Setup.content:
# Output Options

Select which results are calculated and stored.

## Common outputs
- Trajectory start/end points
- Collision events
- Range / lateral distributions
- Backscattered / transmitted energy and angle

> Hint: Enabling fewer outputs can reduce runtime and file size.

Single Plot.title: Curves
Single Plot.content:
# Curves

The overlay shows one or more curves; each can be styled independently.

## Loading curves
- **Double-click a plot tile** on the MC Results tab to append all of its visible series here. Existing curves stay.
- Or use **Load Output Directory** to read a previous simulation.

## Managing the list
- Tick/untick a curve to toggle its **visibility**.
- **Remove** drops the selected curve; **Clear All** empties the list.
- Select a curve to edit its style, convolution and stats on the right.

> Hint: The selected curve is the target for the Selected Curve, Gaussian Convolution and Stats panels.

Single Plot.title: Load Output Directory
Single Plot.content:
# Load Output Directory

Load curves directly from a previous simulation output directory instead of the MC Results tab.

## Steps
- Click **Load Output Directory…** and pick a folder.
- All `.his` series found there are listed in the **Dataset** dropdown.
- Choose a dataset to append its curves to the plot.

> Hint: Use this to compare results from earlier runs side by side.

Single Plot.title: Selected Curve
Single Plot.content:
# Selected Curve

Per-curve matplotlib styling for the curve selected in the Curves list.

## Options
- **Label**: legend text for the curve.
- **Color**: line/marker color.
- **Line style & width**, **marker** and **opacity**.
- **Z-order**: drawing order (higher is on top).

> Hint: Styling applies only to the currently selected curve.

Single Plot.title: Gaussian Convolution
Single Plot.content:
# Gaussian Convolution

Folds the selected curve with a Gaussian to mimic finite beam/detector resolution.

## Depth profiles
- **Beam σ (Å)**: Gaussian width in plot units. The curve is convolved with `exp(−x²/2σ²)`.
- When you first enable convolution with σ still at 0, a default of **~3 % of the curve's x-range** is filled in so the effect is immediately visible.

## Lateral / 2-D curves
- **Scan area** (min–max) applies a rectangular scan along the lateral axis, convolved with the Gaussian via an error-function kernel.
- Negative bounds are allowed, since the lateral axis is symmetric around 0.

## Applying
- Set σ (and scan area) first, then tick **Apply convolution** at the bottom of the panel.

> Hint: Load and select a curve before enabling convolution.

Single Plot.title: Axes & Legend
Single Plot.content:
# Axes & Legend

Global axis and legend settings for the whole plot.

## Options
- **Title** and **X / Y labels** (including secondary top/right axes).
- **Log X / Log Y** scaling (primary and secondary axes).
- **Grid** and **Legend** toggles, plus legend **position**.

> Hint: Labels are auto-filled from the loaded data but can be overridden; your edits take precedence.

Single Plot.title: Reference Image
Single Plot.content:
# Reference Image

Overlay a bitmap under the curves to compare against an external figure (e.g. a micrograph or a plot from an earlier run).

## Options
- **Load Image…**: pick a JPEG/PNG to draw beneath the curves.
- **Opacity**: blend the image with the plot background.
- **Clear Image**: remove the overlay.

> Hint: Align the image by matching the axis ranges to the image extent.
